metering_mechanism.source: services/api/app/services/freshness_integration.py Attempt.install_browser / admit / request_bytes; services/api/app/services/freshness_queue.py admit_request, claim_due, complete_claim
metering_mechanism.unit: One grant (cost=1) per Playwright route callback that is actually dispatched via route.fetch, i.e. per outgoing request, BEFORE the network call. Each explicit asset redirect hop is another grant. Main-frame redirects are refused. Artwork bytes (SNKR) are separately metered via request_bytes (1 grant each). WebSockets closed, service workers blocked.
metering_mechanism.not_metered: Requests aborted by unnecessary_browser_resource(): resource_type image/font/media, ADVERTISING_HOSTS (googletagmanager, doubleclick, googleadservices, facebook, ads-twitter, t.co, criteo, rentracks), google.com/measurement/conversion, bbc.bibian.co.jp, snkrdunk.com GET /v1/accounts/me. Also anything after browser_closing.
metering_mechanism.budget_accounting: claim_due reserves work.estimated_request_cost (refresh 300, Yuyu discovery 1200) into source_dispatch_budgets.reserved_requests; admission requires estimate <= request_limit - used - reserved; admit_request refuses ordinals beyond the reservation; complete_claim moves reserved -> used_requests += actual_request_cost (expired claims charged full reservation). Window: fixed 1800s, used reset on rollover.
metering_mechanism.http_cache: context.route('**/*') is installed for every freshness context; Playwright disables the HTTP cache when routing is enabled, so every page re-requests all its scripts/styles even inside one context (relevant to option 1 and option 4).
metering_mechanism.classification: browser_request_role: main-frame navigation=required_document(critical); script/stylesheet/document(iframe)=optional_presentation; EVERYTHING ELSE (xhr/fetch/other, any host incl. third-party) = required_application (critical: a 403/429 pauses the source).

4_followup_turn_scoped_static_cache.note: Because routing disables the browser cache, a normal visitor would NOT re-request identical hashed scripts/styles on every product page. A per-turn in-memory cache honoring Cache-Control for GET 200 script/stylesheet responses would emulate ordinary caching (no network dispatch -> no grant). Level-1 product assets are 100% identical across product pages (MEASURED).
